info.title: Brief! API
info.description:
Backend for **Brief!**, a message board where every post fits in 255 characters.

The same API is served by two editions of the backend: **Javalin + JDBC** (`backend/`) and **Spring Boot + Spring Security + Spring Data JPA** (`backend-spring/`).

**How errors work:** error responses have an empty body. The status code carries the meaning.

**How to try the protected endpoints here:**
1. Run `POST /register` to create an account (or use one you already have).
2. Run `POST /login`. In the response headers, copy the value of `x-auth-token`.
3. Click **Authorize** at the top right, paste the token, and confirm.
4. Now `POST`, `PATCH` and `DELETE` on `/messages` will work, as that account.

The app runs in *strict* mode by default: you can only post as yourself and only change your own posts. Set the environment variable `BRIEF_AUTH_MODE=compat` before starting to get the original training contract, where no token is needed.

**New in 2.1 (Spring Boot edition only):** the login token is a signed JWT; `GET /messages` and `GET /accounts/{account_id}/messages` can be read a page at a time with `limit` and `before`; in strict mode new passwords must be strong and repeated failed logins answer `429`. The Javalin edition ignores the paging parameters and always returns the full list.

**New in 2.2 (Spring Boot edition only):** mentions are stored in their own indexed table when a post is saved or edited, so `GET /accounts/{account_id}/mentions` is a look-up and no longer searches every post.

**New in 2.3 (Spring Boot edition only):** `GET /accounts/{account_id}/mentions` can be read a page at a time with `limit` and `before`, like the other lists; a username is one name whatever its capitals, for registering and for signing in; in strict mode a new username must be 3 to 30 letters, digits, dots, dashes or underscores. The database schema is created by versioned Flyway migrations, and the application runs on PostgreSQL as well as H2.

**New in 2.4 (Spring Boot edition only):** an account has an email address. In strict mode a new account must give one, and can read but not post until the link mailed to it has been opened (`POST /email/verify`). A forgotten password is replaced through a mailed link (`POST /password/forgot`, `POST /password/reset`). An address is shown only to its own account (`GET /me`). A board can be **closed** (`BRIEF_BOARD=closed`; in 2.4 `BRIEF_INVITE_CODE`): creating an account then needs an invitation, and every `GET` of posts and members needs a login token. `GET /health` reports `email` and `board`, so a client knows which of this applies.

**New in 2.5 (Spring Boot edition only):** newcomers to a closed board join through **invitation links** that the board owner (`BRIEF_OWNER_USERNAME`) mails (`POST /invitations`) or passes on (`POST /invitations/link`). The link opens the web app at `/?invite=<secret>`; `POST /invitations/lookup` tells who sent it, and `POST /register` with `"invitation"` uses it. A mailed invitation creates the account with its address already confirmed. The shared code of 2.4 is no longer asked for. A member can delete their account and posts (`POST /accounts/{account_id}/deletion`). `GET /me` reports `is_owner`.

**New in 2.6:** no change to the API. The web app gains a Help Center (`/help/index.html`): plain pages about what Brief! is, getting started, pricing, an FAQ and the refund policy, public on a closed board like the Terms and Privacy pages.

**New in 2.7 (Spring Boot edition only):** Brief! learns when a mail could not be delivered. Resend reports bounces and suppressed sends to `POST /webhooks/resend`, signed with `BRIEF_RESEND_WEBHOOK_SECRET`. `GET /me` reports `email_bounced`; for a day after a bounce the address is not mailed, and the requests that would mail it answer `422`. The owner's list of invitations shows `bounced` and `taken`. Confirmation and password links are used up in one database statement, so a link works once even when it is opened twice at the same moment.

**New in 2.8 (Spring Boot edition only):** sessions are kept in the database. `POST /login` takes an optional `"stay": true` ("Stay signed in on this device"): the session then lasts 30 days from its last use, at most a year; without it, 12 hours. Signing out ends a session for good, also across restarts. `GET /sessions` lists where a member is signed in; `DELETE /sessions/{session_id}` and `POST /sessions/sign-out-others` end sessions. **Notifications:** with `BRIEF_VAPID_PUBLIC_KEY` and `BRIEF_VAPID_PRIVATE_KEY` set, a member's browser can subscribe (`POST /push/subscription`, with the server key from `GET /push/key`), and receives an encrypted Web Push notification (RFC 8030, 8291, 8292) when a post newly mentions them. `GET /health` reports `sessions` and `push`.

post.description:
Succeeds only if the username is allowed, the password meets the rule, and the username is not taken. The password is stored as a salted hash.

Username rule: not blank. In the Spring Boot edition in strict mode (since 2.3): 3 to 30 characters, each a letter a-z or A-Z, a digit, a dot, a dash or an underscore.

Since 2.3 (Spring Boot edition) a username is one name whatever its capitals: if `Maya` exists, `maya` and `MAYA` are taken. The name is stored and shown as it was typed.

Password rule: at least 4 characters. In the Spring Boot edition in strict mode: at least 8 characters, with at least one letter and one digit, and not the same as the username. `GET /health` reports which rule applies.

Since 2.4 (Spring Boot edition): in strict mode an `email` is required and must not belong to another account. A link is mailed to it; until it is used the account can sign in and read, and cannot post.

Since 2.5: on a closed board (`GET /health` says `"board": "closed"`) the request must carry a usable `invitation`; without one the answer is `403` whatever else the request holds, and five bad ones from one address lock that address out for 15 minutes. A mailed invitation fixes the address and confirms it: no confirmation mail is sent.

400.description: Invalid input, a username, password or email address that does not meet the rule, or a username (in any capitals) or email address that is already taken. Empty body. Since 2.5 also: an address other than the one a mailed invitation was sent to.

403.description: Closed board: no invitation, or one that was used, withdrawn or expired (on an open board: a given invitation that is not usable). Empty body.

429.description: Too many bad invitations from this address. `Retry-After` says how many seconds to wait. Empty body.

422.description: Since 2.7: the email given bounced in the last day (most likely a typo). Empty body.

post.description:
Checks the username and password. Since 2.3 (Spring Boot edition) the username is matched whatever capitals are typed; the answer carries it as it was registered. The password is always exact. On success the response carries a login token in the `X-Auth-Token` header; send it back as `Authorization: Bearer <token>` on write requests.

In the Spring Boot edition the token is a JWT signed with HMAC-SHA256. Its payload holds the account id (`sub`), a token id (`jti`), the issue and expiry times, and since 2.4 the account's token generation (`ver`); it is readable by anyone and holds nothing secret.

In strict mode (Spring Boot edition), five wrong passwords for the same username from the same address lock that pair out for 15 minutes. Behind a hosting platform's proxy the address is read from the header named in `BRIEF_CLIENT_IP_HEADER` (since 2.3).

Since 2.4 a token also stops working when the account's password is replaced through a mailed link: every session of that account ends at that moment.

X-Auth-Token.description: Login token, valid for 12 hours or until logout.

401.description: Username and password do not match. Empty body.

429.description: Too many failed attempts for this username from this address (Spring Boot edition, strict mode). Empty body.

Retry-After.description: Seconds until a login may be tried again.

post.description: Ends the session for the token sent. Since 2.8 the session is deleted from the database, so the token is refused from then on, also after a restart, and the device's notifications stop. Always answers 200, even if the token is already gone (idempotent).

get.description:
Posts written by other members that contain this member's username as a whole word, in any letter case, with or without a leading `@`. A member's own posts never count.

Without query parameters: every mention, oldest first.

Spring Boot edition, since 2.3: with `limit` and/or `before`, one page, **newest first**, and an `X-Has-More` header, exactly like `GET /messages`. The web app reads 20 at a time. The Javalin edition ignores the parameters and returns the full list.

Spring Boot edition, since 2.2: who a post mentions is worked out when the post is saved or edited and stored in a `mention` table, so this request is an indexed look-up. One consequence: a name typed before that member registered is not a mention. The Javalin edition searches every post at request time.

On a closed board (since 2.4, Spring Boot edition) this needs a login token; on an open board it is public.

200.description: The mentioning messages: all of them oldest first, or one page newest first. An empty list if there are none.

X-Has-More.description: Only when `limit` or `before` was sent: `true` if older mentions exist beyond this page, otherwise `false`.

400.description: The id is not a number, or a paging parameter is out of range. Empty body.

401.description: Closed board (since 2.4): no token, or one that is unknown or expired. Empty body.

200.description: The posts. An empty list if there are none.

X-Has-More.description: Only when `limit` or `before` was sent: `true` if older posts exist beyond this page, otherwise `false`.

400.description: `limit` is not between 1 and 100, or `before` is not a positive number. Empty body.

401.description: Closed board (since 2.4): no token, or one that is unknown or expired. Empty body.

get.description:
Without parameters: every post, oldest first (the original contract).

With `limit` and/or `before` (Spring Boot edition): one page, **newest first**, and an `X-Has-More` response header. To walk the whole list, call with `limit`, then repeat with `before` set to the `message_id` of the last post you received, until `X-Has-More` is `false`.

On a closed board (since 2.4, Spring Boot edition) this needs a login token; on an open board it is public.

On success every login token of the account issued before stops working. A password that is refused does not use the link up.

get.description: `password_policy` is sent by the Spring Boot edition: `strong` in strict mode, `basic` in compat mode. Since 2.4 it also sends `email` (`required` in strict mode, `optional` in compat mode) and `board` (`closed` or `open`, from `BRIEF_BOARD`). The Javalin edition sends only `status`. This endpoint is public on a closed board too. Since 2.8 also `sessions` (`kept`: sessions live in the database) and `push` (`on` when notifications can be turned on).

post.description: Since 2.7 (Spring Boot edition). Called by Resend, not by members: no login token. The call must be signed as Svix signs webhooks (headers `svix-id`, `svix-timestamp`, `svix-signature`; HMAC-SHA256 of `id.timestamp.body` with the secret `BRIEF_RESEND_WEBHOOK_SECRET`) and be at most five minutes old. Brief! acts on `email.bounced` (permanent only) and `email.suppressed`, for mail sent from its own domain; every other event is acknowledged and ignored. Each `svix-id` is handled once; a body over 256 KB is refused.

parameters.name: svix-signature
parameters.description: One or more `v1,<base64>`, separated by spaces.

schema.description: A Resend event: `type` and `data` (with `to`, `from`, and for bounces `bounce.type`).

200.description: Recorded, or nothing to record. Empty body.

400.description: Signed, but not a JSON event. Empty body.

401.description: Signature headers missing (refused before the body is read), or signature wrong or older than five minutes. Empty body.

404.description: `BRIEF_RESEND_WEBHOOK_SECRET` is not set on this server. Empty body.

409.description: Two reports about one new address arrived at once; Resend sends this one again. Empty body.

413.description: The body is larger than 256 KB. Empty body.

get.description: 2.8. The caller's sessions that have not ended, newest first. `current` marks the one this request was made with (none for a token issued before 2.8).

401.description: No valid token.

delete.description: 2.8. Ends one of the caller's sessions, and with it that device's notifications.

401.description: No valid token.

404.description: No such session, or someone else's (the same answer).

post.description: 2.8. Ends every session of the caller except this one, and every token from before 2.8. This session's token is replaced too: the answer carries a new one in `x-auth-token`, for the same session; use it from now on.

x-auth-token.description: The new token for this session.

401.description: No valid token.

409.description: The token is from before 2.8 and belongs to no session: sign in again first.

get.description: 2.8. Brief!'s VAPID public key (RFC 8292), the `applicationServerKey` for `PushManager.subscribe`. Public, also on a closed board.

404.description: Notifications are off on this server (no VAPID keys).

post.summary: Turn on notifications for this device
post.description: 2.8. Stores the browser's subscription with the caller's current session. From then on a post that newly mentions the caller sends an encrypted notification to it. Signing that session out deletes it.

400.description: The endpoint is not at a known push service, or the keys are not a P-256 key and a 16-byte secret.

409.description: The token is from before 2.8 and belongs to no session: sign in again first.

401.description: No valid token.

404.description: Notifications are off on this server.

200.description: `on` is true if this endpoint is stored for the caller's current session.

401.description: No valid token.

post.summary: Turn off notifications for this device

200.description: Forgotten, if it was the caller's. Empty body.

401.description: No valid token.

post.description: 2.8. Sends a test notification to the devices of the caller's current session.

409.description: The token belongs to no session.

429.description: A test was sent less than a minute ago. See Retry-After.

401.description: No valid token.

404.description: Notifications are off on this server.

bearerAuth.description: Paste the `x-auth-token` value from a successful `POST /login`.

password.description: At least 4 characters; in the Spring Boot edition in strict mode at least 8 with a letter and a digit.

stay.description: 2.8, optional, `POST /login` only: true for a session that lasts 30 days from its last use ("Stay signed in on this device"); absent or false, 12 hours.

Account.description: The contract echoes back the password the caller sent. It is never read back from the database, which only holds a hash.

example.message_text: Not really, I just want to come in and see who's up to chat!

time_posted_epoch.description: Seconds since 1970-01-01 UTC. Send 0 to let the server fill it in.

password.description: At least 4 characters; in the Spring Boot edition in strict mode at least 8 with a letter and a digit.

email.description: Since 2.4 (Spring Boot edition). Required in strict mode, optional in compat mode. Stored in lower case. Do not send it to the Javalin edition.

invitation.description: Since 2.5 (Spring Boot edition). The secret from an invitation link (the text after `?invite=`). Needed on a closed board; optional on an open one, but refused (403) if given and not usable. With a mailed invitation `email` may be left out, and must otherwise be the invited address.

email.description: null for an account that has not given an address.

can_post.description: false in strict mode while an address is waiting to be confirmed.

is_owner.description: Since 2.5: true for the member who runs the board and can invite people.

email_bounced.description: Since 2.7: true while mail to the address is known to bounce. The web app then asks for a different address.

token.description: The secret from the mailed link: the text after `?verify=` or `?reset=`.
The secret from the mailed link: the text after `?reset=`.

email.description: null for a link that was passed on.

status.description: Since 2.7 also `bounced` (the mail could not be delivered) and `taken` (the address now belongs to a member, so the invitation can no longer create an account).

joined_as.description: The username of the account created with it, while it exists.

expires_at.description: When the session ends unless it is used again (for a stay session).

current.description: The session this request was made with.

PushSubscription.description: What the browser's `PushSubscription.toJSON()` gives. `expirationTime` and other fields are ignored.

endpoint.description: https, at a browser maker's push service (Google, Mozilla, Apple, Microsoft); anything else is refused (400).

p256dh.description: The browser's P-256 public key, base64url.
